summary.headline: Welspun Enterprises Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 32% YoY to INR1,035 crores and EBITDA 122% to INR425 crores, aided by a INR194 crore Mukarba Chowk-Panipat stake sale gain.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was INR1,035 crores (up 32% YoY) and EBITDA INR425 crores (up 122%), with a 39.5% margin that includes a INR194 crore gain from completing the 51% stake divestment of the Mukarba Chowk-Panipat road project. Excluding that gain, management said margins are still above 20%. H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,808 crores (up 11%) and EBITDA INR610 crores (up 53%), with management calling H2 stronger than H1. Welspun Michigan (WMEL) revenue fell year on year in H1 due to delayed order releases, which management described as phasing. The company also announced a DGH approval for toll-based use of ONGC facilities for its Mumbai block gas.

financial_highlights.value: INR3,581 crores / INR1,432 crores / INR450 crores

segments.name: Welspun Michigan Engineers (WMEL)
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR139 crores, EBITDA INR25 crores, PAT INR12 crores; H1 revenue INR318 crores, EBITDA INR63 crores, PAT INR35 crores. Order book INR2,279 crores (tunneling 53%, pumping 21%, rehabilitation 19%), about 3 years of run-rate revenue.

segments.name: Transportation
segments.commentary: Aunta-Simaria road divestment expected to be reflected in Q3 FY27. Varanasi-Aurangabad road completed and awaiting provisional completion certificate; Sattanathapuram-Nagapattinam 90% complete. Pune-Shirur debt sanction of INR6,334 crores from Union Bank of India and PNB.

segments.name: Water
segments.commentary: Dharavi 418 MLD plant on track for commissioning by July 2027, followed by a 15-year O&M contract. UP Jal Jeevan Mission over 80% physical completion, with over 450 of 1,068 schemes completed or in trial/O&M.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 10% to 20%, reaffirmed; management said it is reasonably confident of being in range.
EBITDA margin guidance of 18% plus, reaffirmed; management declined to specify how far above 18% it expects to be.

Incremental order inflow of INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores in FY27, almost entirely expected in H2 and mainly water, with some rehabilitation and tunneling and transportation orders from year-end.
Pune-Shirur appointed date expected by Q4 FY27; FY27 revenue from the project INR300 crores to INR400 crores; FY28 revenue INR1,000 crores to INR1,200 crores.

WMEL FY27 order additions of INR700 crores to INR1,200 crores expected; medium-term guidance of 15% to 20% revenue growth and EBITDA margin above 20% unchanged, though management called FY27 a temporary blip.
Aunta-Simaria divestment: equity of about INR200 crores plus NCA, with INR764 crores of debt transferring.
capex_capacity: Pune-Shirur: casting yards at 2 locations, design progressing, test piling begun; financial closure and appointed date expected by Q4 FY27.
Dharavi Wastewater 418 MLD plant: commissioning targeted July 2027.
Bhandup 2,000 MLD water treatment plant: excavation and civil works under way after civil contractor mobilization; execution slowed by debris disposal limits and BMC air-quality suspensions.
Panjarpur 910 MLD plant: mobilization done, excavation started, completion targeted April 2030.
Dharavi-Ghatkopar tunnel: Ghatkopar shaft at 26 metres, completion by FY33. PST-1 tunnel due September 2027, PST-2 (4.6 km) January 2028, Mithi tunnel (about INR400 crores) January 2028.
demand_pricing: WMEL order inflow of about INR450 crores in the quarter to date from 3 rehabilitation projects and 1 micro-tunneling project, including 2 World Bank-funded Ahmedabad pipeline projects and an NDMC pipeline project.
WMEL bidding pipeline of INR1,500 crores to INR1,800 crores, pursued with margin discipline.

Oil and gas: DGH approved toll-based use of ONGC facilities (B-12-11P, TCPP, SBHT pipeline, Hazira) for the Mumbai block; revised early development plan submitted to DGH, approval awaited. Capex estimated to fall by USD300-400 million; resource base about 0.6 Tcf gas and 2 million barrels of oil/condensate; early revenue targeted FY29. Revenue and investment not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Details of the ONGC arrangement, roles, capex, and expected revenue, profitability and margin for the oil and gas division.
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave the infrastructure route but withheld investment and revenue figures pending DGH approval of the EDP. Capex is expected to fall by USD300-400 million versus the original longer pipeline plan.

qa_highlights.question: Will WMEL reach its INR1,000 crore revenue expectation given H1 of about INR320 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the shortfall to order-release timing that pushed execution into later periods. It expects FY27 to be a growth year over FY26 but would not commit to beating last year's revenue by 5% or more.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the Chinese export ban on tunnel boring machines on WMEL.
qa_highlights.answer: WMEL has not bought Chinese TBMs and sources from Japan and Germany, both with Thailand and India operations; Herrenknecht has a large factory in Tamil Nadu. Management sees no impact on execution.

qa_highlights.question: Consolidated order inflow and sector mix for FY27 and the Pune-Shirur revenue outlook.
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed INR8,000-10,000 crores of inflow, mainly water, with transportation orders from year-end. Pune-Shirur revenue is INR300-400 crores in FY27 and INR1,000-1,200 crores in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Whether the 10-20% revenue growth guidance and 18%-plus margin guidance still hold after H1.
qa_highlights.answer: Management reaffirmed both, citing H1 typically at about 40% of annual revenue. Margins ex-MCP gain are above 20%, but it would not specify how far above 18% it expects to be.

qa_highlights.question: Aunta-Simaria deal terms.
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to about INR200 crores of equity plus NCA, with INR764 crores of debt transferring to the buyer.

risks_watch: Q2 margin of 39.5% includes a INR194 crore one-off divestment gain; underlying H2 margin must hold at 18%-plus.
FY27 needs INR8,000-10,000 crores of order inflow, almost all in H2; any spillover would weigh on the target.
WMEL H1 revenue of INR318 crores versus expectations of about INR1,000 crores; FY27 execution depends on ramp-up of released orders.
Mumbai water projects (Bhandup) affected by debris disposal limits and BMC air-quality suspensions.
Pune-Shirur revenue depends on financial closure and appointed date by Q4 FY27.
Oil and gas EDP approval from DGH is pending; capex and revenue remain undisclosed.
summary.management_tone: Confident on H2 and guidance, but evasive on specifics: management declined to quantify oil and gas investment and revenue, and the WMEL FY27 revenue target, citing confidentiality and pending approvals.
key_quotes: Historically, H2 has always been better period than H1. So the H1 numbers should be seen as a base on which the second half shall build.
We are absolutely confident of making 18% plus, whether the plus will be 2% or 4%, I don't know at this point in time, and I would not want to comment upon it at this stage.
This specific order, allows us to move a substantial investment of capital, avoid it and move it to more of a revenue expense, thus, it derisks the business in totality.

adds.what: Pune-Shirur road project (appointed date and financial closure expected by Q4 FY27)

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 10% to 20% (midpoint 15%, held) and EBITDA margin 18%+; delivery relies on INR8,000-10,000 crore order inflow almost entirely in H2 and Pune-Shirur revenue of INR300-400 crore in FY27, but H1 revenue grew only 11% and Q2 growth is inflated by a INR194 crore one-off divestment gain.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin 39.5% includes INR194 crore MCP divestment gain; ex-gain margins still above 20% and FY27 guided at 18%+, but H1 margin 32.4% is flattered by the one-off, so underlying H2 margin must hold at 18%+ rather than expand.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Pune-Shirur appointed date and financial closure expected by Q4 FY27 with FY28 revenue of INR1,000-1,200 crore, and Dharavi 418 MLD commissioning targeted July 2027, so new road and water capacity comes live in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 10-20% (H1 only +11%) and INR8,000-10,000 crore order inflow expected almost entirely in H2, with WMEL FY27 order additions of INR700-1,200 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Pune-Shirur financial closure is due by Q4 FY27 and Mumbai oil and gas EDP approval from DGH is pending with capex cut by USD300-400 million, but utilisation was not disclosed so there is no direct capacity-stress signal.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reaffirmed 10-20% revenue growth and 18%+ margin and declined to say how far above 18% it expects, while H1 revenue grew only 11% and WMEL H1 revenue was INR318 crore against an expected ~INR1,000 crore, so no clear upgrade trigger.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 needs INR8,000-10,000 crore of order inflow almost all in H2, WMEL revenue is behind, and Bhandup execution is slowed by BMC suspensions, so any spillover into FY28 would weigh on the target.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Mumbai block gas via ONGC facilities has DGH approval for toll-based use, with early revenue targeted FY29, but the revised EDP is still awaiting approval and no figures were disclosed.

rows.label: WMEL order inflow and bidding pipeline
rows.why: About INR450 crore of WMEL orders won quarter to date and a INR1,500-1,800 crore bidding pipeline, against a INR2,279 crore order book of about 3 years run-rate revenue.

rows.label: Aunta-Simaria divestment reflected in Q3 FY27
rows.why: Equity of about INR200 crore plus NCA, with INR764 crore of debt transferring to the buyer, is expected to reflect in Q3 FY27 after the MCP divestment already completed.

rows.label: Pune-Shirur debt sanction
rows.why: Debt sanction of INR6,334 crore from Union Bank of India and PNB is already in place, with financial closure needed by Q4 FY27 to start revenue.

tone.note: Management was confident on H2 order inflow, the 10-20% growth and 18%+ margin guidance, and Pune-Shirur, but evasive on oil and gas capex and revenue and on the WMEL FY27 revenue target, while analysts pressed on WMEL's shortfall and whether guidance holds after H1.
